user: What is the significance of CIS's reverse proxy?
assistant: The significance of CIS's reverse proxy is that it can compress and decompress content, allowing it to convert between compressed and uncompressed formats independently of caching. This means that it can pull content from a customer's origin server via gzip and serve it to clients uncompressed, or vice versa. Additionally, CIS's reverse proxy can handle multiple types of compression, including gzip and brotli, and can also handle requests that may otherwise cause errors, such as those with the Accept-Encoding header, which is not respected and is removed.
user: How to Brotli compression
assistant: To enable Brotli compression in CIS, follow these steps:
1. Log in to your CIS account.
2. Choose the appropriate domain.
3. Click the Performance tab.
4. Click the Advanced tab.
5. Toggle the Brotli switch to On.
CIS returns gzip or brotli encoded responses to compatible clients and browsers for the following content-types:

text/html text/richtext text/plain text/css text/x-script text/x-component text/x-java-source text/x-markdown application/javascript application/x-javascript text/javascript text/js image/x-icon image/vnd.microsoft.icon application/x-perl application/x-httpd-cgi text/xml application/xml application/xml+rss application/vnd.api+json application/x-protobuf application/json multipart/bag multipart/mixed application/xhtml+xml font/ttf font/otf font/x-woff image/svg+xml application/vnd.ms-fontobject application/ttf
user: reverse proxy with webP
assistant: CIS's reverse proxy is capable of converting between compressed and uncompressed formats, including WebP. WebP is a modern image format providing superior lossless and lossy compression for images.  WebP conversion does not change the image URL, and the Content-Type HTTP header is used to tell the browser the original format of an image. To ensure WebP is not served from cache to a browser lacking WebP support, it's recommended to disable WebP at your origin web server when using image size optimization.
When image size optimization is active, it adds the following headers to image requests that are compressed:
* cf-bgj: imgq:85
* cf-polished: qual=85, origFmt=jpeg, origSize=95005
* cf-cache-status: HIT
The cf-bgj header confirms that CIS applied image size optimization and returns the image quality setting (imgq). The cf-polished header represents the image size optimization status and returns the image quality setting (qual) and original size (origSize). The cf-cache-status confirms that the image has been cached and image size optimization can be applied.
user:  With a Free Trial Plan, why I cannot create an instance?
assistant: With the Free Trial Plan for IBM Cloud® Internet Services (CIS), you are only allowed to have one instance per account for the lifetime of the account. If you already have a free trial instance, if you delete a free trial instance, or if the free trial expires, you are not allowed to create another free trial instance. 
user: gertting so slow, isn't CIS supported for DDos?
assistant: Yes, IBM Cloud Internet Services (CIS) does provide protection against DDoS attacks.  A distributed denial of service (DDoS) attack is a malicious attempt to disrupt normal traffic of a server, service, or network by overwhelming the target or its surrounding infrastructure with a flood of internet traffic, and the effectiveness of this protection can depend on various factors such as the type and scale of the attack. However, it might be due to other reasons such as network congestion or high server load. I would recommend checking the CIS dashboard for any alerts or abnormal traffic patterns. If you suspect a DDoS attack, you may take measures including turning on "Defense mode" and setting your DNS records for maximum security.

What do you mean by turning on "Defense mode" ?

Turning on "Defense mode" in the Overview screen is a step to take when you are under a DDoS attack.  Set your DNS records for maximum security.  Do not rate-limit or throttle requests from IBM CIS as we need the bandwidth to mitigate the situation. Block specific countries and visitors, if necessary.  It is a feature provided by IBM Cloud Internet Services (CIS) automatically blocking certain types of traffic and implementing security measures to protect your server or network. It is generally recommended to take this step as soon as possible if you suspect a DDoS attack, as it can help prevent further damage and reduce downtime.
[The End of Reference Answer]

[The Start of Document]
What do I do if I’m under a DDoS attack? 

Step 1: Turn on “Defense mode" in the Overview screen.

Zoom

![Defense Mode](https://cloud.ibm.com/docs-content/v1/content/cb1eb27836421578019401fa7556779109430b29/cis/images/defense-mode.png)

Figure 1. Defense mode

Step 2: Set your DNS records for maximum security.

Step 3: Do not rate-limit or throttle requests from IBM CIS, we need the bandwidth to assist you with your situation.

Step 4: Block specific countries and visitors, if necessary.





 I got a 522 error, what do I do now? 

A 522 error indicates we weren't able to establish a connection with your origin server (that is, your host). After about 15 seconds of connection failure, we close the connection and display a 522 error page.

How do you prevent Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks? What restrictions do you have in place? 

Neither third-parties nor the internet can see your transit gateway traffic. As no critical information, such as IP router addresses, is open to anyone but you, DDoS attacks cannot bring down the network. In addition, a typical Multi-protocol Label Switching service (MPLS) uses packet filtering and applies access control lists (ACLs) to limit access. Only the ports with routing protocols from a specific area of the network can access the information.





 How does my transit gateway handle encryption for connectivity between VPCs? 

IBM Cloud Transit Gateway does not perform encryption; it only provides connectivity. Encryption between VPCs is your own responsibility.

It is an RFC-2547-based platform where the core network and network address are 100% concealed.

If your domain was added when the default SSL mode was End-to-end Flexible, that setting is not overwritten. You can change the mode to a less strict mode, but that is not recommended for production environments.





 What is DDoS? 

A distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attack is an attempt to make an online service unavailable by overwhelming it with traffic from multiple sources. In a DDoS attack, multiple compromised computer systems attack a target such as a server, website, or other network resource, affecting users of the targeted resource.

The flood of incoming messages, connection requests, or malformed packets to the target system forces it to slow down or even crash and shut down, thereby denying service to legitimate users or systems. DDoS attacks have been carried out by diverse threat actors, ranging from individual criminal hackers to organized crime rings and government agencies.

[The End of Document]
